mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stops falling and remains near flat or positive for two consecutive weeks, weekday foot traffic and discretionary shopping recover with a lag, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -5.3 to -8.1 over the snapshot while RETAIL_REC stayed near -12
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 4 weeks after WORKPLACES turns flat or positive for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, at-home substitution suppresses shopping trips; if RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and does not decelerate, RETAIL_REC will stay lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 for at least 2 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +5 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases access to retail corridors and generates spillover errands; when both series improve together, RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks more than either series alone would imply.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -10.6 to -5.7 before weakening; WORKPLACES briefly turned positive
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops sharply below its recent range, retail access becomes harder and spontaneous trips fall; a week-on-week transit decline of more than 3 points should be followed by weaker RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -5.7 to -8.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 7 days after a transit drop larger than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-summer leisure regime, rising PARKS mobility competes with shopping time; continued PARKS strength diverts discretionary trips away from retail and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -37.1 to -24.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises materially while PARKS continues improving for four consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains strongly positive while RESIDENTIAL also stays elevated, households consolidate errands and shorten nonessential shopping trips; the combined effect lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed above +10 in all weeks while RESIDENTIAL stayed above +6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above +10 and RESIDENTIAL staying above +6.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, a fresh drop in WORKPLACES below zero signals reduced in-person activity and weaker retail demand; once WORKPLACES turns negative after being positive, RETAIL_REC should fall within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses from positive to negative
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was +1.3 at t-1w and -8.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES crosses from positive to negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS and TRANSIT together indicates broader out-of-home activity that carries into retail visits; if both series improve simultaneously, RETAIL_REC will improve over the next four weeks even if current retail mobility is still negative.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -37.1 to -24.0 while TRANSIT stayed negative but recovered earlier
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or worsens over 28 days despite simultaneous improvement in PARKS and TRANSIT.
